mbm-0876.clue: I can crochet faster than our kettle.
mbm-0876.quote: My sister times tea by the rows in my scarf. Last Tuesday we started talking and our tea went completely cold. The scarf gained a bright yellow stripe longer than my arm.

mbm-0877.clue: I collect the buttons with jobs to do.
mbm-0877.quote: I sewed a coat for my niece with a different button for each pocket. She keeps seashells behind the blue fish and one emergency peppermint behind the red apple.

mbm-0878.clue: I have a paper bird that opens the curtains.
mbm-0878.quote: I cut a swallow from red paper and folded its wings around the curtain tie. Every morning I unhook the wings and let the little bird fly across the window.

mbm-0879.clue: I’ve got a mountain under my breakfast plate.
mbm-0879.quote: My dad carved our favorite ski run into the edge of a wooden tray. I run a finger down the sharp turn at breakfast. Half the family thinks it’s decoration.

mbm-0880.clue: I knew we were close when I heard the cup.
mbm-0880.quote: My hiking partner hangs an enamel cup outside her pack. The little clink went quiet at the ridge. When I caught up she had filled it with blackberries for me.

mbm-0881.clue: I don’t own the green jacket.
mbm-0881.quote: My aunt lends me her lucky green cardigan whenever we play nine holes. The sleeves reach my knuckles. I roll them up twice and she says that’s the real secret to my swing.

mbm-0882.clue: My loudest puppet fits in my pocket.
mbm-0882.quote: I stitched a little dumpling seller with enormous eyebrows for our glove-puppet show. When I waggle one eyebrow the children shout their orders before I even give him a voice.

mbm-0883.clue: I polish the orange ball twice.
mbm-0883.quote: Our bowling coach taught me using an orange ball with one white swirl. If I release smoothly the swirl draws a little ribbon down the lane. I watch the ribbon all the way to the pins.

mbm-0884.clue: I practice the turn beside a broom closet.
mbm-0884.quote: My ballroom partner and I found a mirror on the back of the community hall closet door. We can check one pair of feet at a time. Mine are finally going in the same direction as hers.

mbm-0885.clue: I leave the chalk flowers until last.
mbm-0885.quote: I traced my sister’s sidewalk daisies onto fabric before a shower washed them away. They grew into a quilt for her first apartment. The yellow flower at the corner still has her crooked stem.

mbm-0886.clue: I’m the custodian of seven green frogs.
mbm-0886.quote: Our quilting circle each stitched a frog from a different green scrap. Mine has one long leg. The seven sit around a blue patchwork pond just like us crowding around the sewing table.

mbm-0887.clue: I always bring my best pair of sticks.
mbm-0887.quote: I marked my claves with a little purple loop of yarn after I mixed them up at a son rehearsal. When the tune picks up, that yarn whirls like a tiny dancer.

mbm-0888.clue: I like the postcard rack behind the station.
mbm-0888.quote: I pick the view upside down and walk until I can turn it upright in front of the real thing. Last weekend I found a stone lion almost hidden behind a flower cart.

mbm-0889.clue: I made a handkerchief stay disappeared.
mbm-0889.quote: The red silk was supposed to come back on command. Our terrier ran off with it. I bowed, called for my assistant and waited while he galloped onstage to wild applause.

mbm-0890.clue: I raised a flag for the sandwiches.
mbm-0890.quote: We lashed a clean napkin to a paddle when our raft reached the picnic bank. The next boat spotted it across the reeds and came drifting in like we’d opened a tiny riverside café.

mbm-0891.clue: I set an extra place outside the tent.
mbm-0891.quote: My sister and I cooked porridge in the rain. We put an empty bowl out to measure the drips, and by breakfast our spare place setting was nearly full.

mbm-0892.clue: I can see the beat on my sneakers.
mbm-0892.quote: I put pearl beads on my dancing shoes. Under the club’s colored lights each step throws tiny moving dots onto the floor. My friend calls it our own little light show.

mbm-0893.clue: I watch the backgrounds at anime club.
mbm-0893.quote: Everybody wanted to draw the giant robot. I drew the tiny flower shop behind its left heel. By the end of the tape the whole club was checking that the shop still stood.

mbm-0894.clue: I once bought a drawer on its own.
mbm-0894.quote: A flea-market seller had one blue drawer with a brass fish for a handle. I took it home and hung it on the wall. The fish now guards my little postcard collection.

mbm-0895.clue: I have a volleyball with a tide mark.
mbm-0895.quote: Our ball floated just past the boundary of seaweed, and my partner waded out after it. We dried it on the picnic blanket. I still see a faint salt line when I serve.

mbm-0896.clue: I keep a fallen rivet on my desk.
mbm-0896.quote: While helping polish an old display plane I found a brass rivet beneath its wheel. The mechanic showed me an identical one in the wing and let me keep the loose one for my paperweight.

mbm-0897.clue: I carry measuring tape for strange furniture.
mbm-0897.quote: A little shelf at the market fit between my kitchen cupboards with half an inch to spare. The seller sent along a toy blue whale. It fits the shelf with exactly the same margin.

mbm-0898.clue: I’ve sewn an orchard that stays in blossom.
mbm-0898.quote: My cousins picked different pink scraps for the flowers on our apple-tree quilt. We hid one bright red apple under a flap. The youngest cousin still checks whether the others have ripened.

mbm-0899.clue: My uncle thinks I've moved a star.
mbm-0899.quote: My uncle taught me the constellations from our back step. I stitched the sky from memory on the back of a quilt for him. He says I moved one star. I say he must have moved the step.

mbm-0900.clue: I know which platform gets the evening light.
mbm-0900.quote: Grandpa and I stood at the far end with a thermos to sketch the red local. He drew the engine and I drew its gold reflection in the empty station windows.
